questions.title: GATE CSE 2013 | Question: 6
questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.questionHtml:
Which one of the following is the tightest upper bound that represents the number of swaps required to sort $n$ numbers using selection sort?

  1. $O(\log n$)
  2. $O(n$)
  3. $O(n \log n$)
  4. $O(n^{2}$)
questions.existingSolutionSnippet: Selection sort does at most one swap per pass, so at most n $-$ 1 swaps.

questions.title: GATE CSE 2013 | Question: 7
questions.subject: Programming and DS
questions.questionHtml:
Which one of the following is the tightest upper bound that represents the time complexity of inserting an object into a binary search tree of $n$ nodes?

  1. $O(1)$
  2. $O(\log n)$
  3. $O(n)$
  4. $O(n \log n)$
questions.existingSolutionSnippet: A BST may be skewed (height n $-$ 1), so insertion may walk all n nodes.

questions.title: GATE CSE 2011 | Question: 48
questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.questionHtml:
Consider the following recursive C function that takes two arguments.

unsigned int foo(unsigned int n, unsigned int r) {
    if (n>0) return ((n%r) + foo(n/r, r));
    else return 0;
}

What is the return value of the function $\text{foo}$ when it is called as $\text{foo(345, 10)}$?

  1. $345$
  2. $12$
  3. $5$
  4. $3$
questions.existingSolutionSnippet:
foo(n, r) adds the digits of n in base r.

foo(345, 10) = 5 + 4 + 3 = 12
